ITEM: US Senator (candidate race)

SIDE id="david-brock-smith" — David Brock Smith, Republican
[1] In his voters' pamphlet statement, Brock Smith lists his occupation as State Senator and small business owner. Excerpt: "State Senator, Small Business Owner" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[2] His pamphlet statement lists prior work as a state representative, county commissioner, small business owner and economic development director. Excerpt: "State Representative, County Commissioner, Small Business Owner/Business Manager, Director-Economic Development" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[3] The Oregon Legislature lists Brock Smith as a Republican senator for District 1, based in Port Orford, and as Senate Deputy Leader. Excerpt: "Republican - District 1 - Port Orford - Deputy Leader" (Oregon State Legislature, https://www.oregonlegislature.gov/SmithD)
[4] Brock Smith's pamphlet statement says he opposed the governor's gas tax and new tax increases. Excerpt: "David fought Kotek's-Gas-Tax, stopped new tax-hikes, and continues his work on eliminating fraud," (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[5] Brock Smith says he works to eliminate fraud and reduce unnecessary government spending. Excerpt: "continues his work on eliminating fraud, while reducing unnecessary government spending." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[6] Brock Smith says he will push for treatment and accountability on homelessness and an end to permanent street camping. Excerpt: "David has and will continue to fight for treatment and accountability, and bring an end to permanent street camping." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[7] Brock Smith says data centers strain Oregon's water, farmland, energy costs and communities. Excerpt: "David is concerned data centers strain Oregon’s water, farmland, energy costs, and communities." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[8] Brock Smith says economic development should help residents rather than burden families. Excerpt: "Economic development must help residents, not burden families." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)

SIDE id="jeff-merkley" — Jeff Merkley, Democrat, incumbent
[9] In his voters' pamphlet statement, Merkley lists his occupation as U.S. Senator for Oregon. Excerpt: "U.S. Senator for Oregon" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[10] His pamphlet statement lists prior government experience as a state representative and Oregon House Speaker. Excerpt: "State Representative; Oregon House Speaker" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[11] His pamphlet statement lists past work with Habitat for Humanity, as a national security analyst and as a small business founder. Excerpt: "Habitat for Humanity; National Security Analyst; Small Business Founder" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[12] His official Senate biography says he was the first in his family to graduate from college, in 1979. Excerpt: "In 1979, he became the first person in his family to graduate from college." (Office of U.S. Senator Jeff Merkley, https://www.merkley.senate.gov/about/)
[13] Merkley's pamphlet statement calls for ending stock trading and the exchange of government favors for investments in the president's companies. Excerpt: "No more stock trading; no more exchanging government favors for investments in Trump's companies." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[14] Merkley says he wants to stop gerrymandering, require paper ballots and end secret campaign funding. Excerpt: "Stop gerrymandering. Require paper ballots. End secret campaign funding." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[15] Merkley proposes banning hedge funds from buying single-family homes. Excerpt: "Ban hedge funds from buying single-family homes." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[16] Merkley says he would stop drug companies from price gouging. Excerpt: "Stop drug companies from price gouging." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[17] Merkley proposes affordable daycare and debt-free trade school and college. Excerpt: "Create affordable daycare and debt-free opportunities for trade school and college." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[18] Merkley calls for a rapid transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy, which he describes as cheaper and cleaner. Excerpt: "Rapidly transition from dirty, expensive fossils to cheaper, cleaner, renewables." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[19] Merkley voted Nay on Senate passage of H.R. 1, the budget reconciliation bill, on July 1, 2025 (Senate roll call vote 372). Excerpt: "On Passage of the Bill (H.R. 1, as Amended) … Merkley (D-OR), Nay" (U.S. Senate, https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote1191/vote_119_1_00372.htm)
[20] Merkley voted Nay on Senate passage of S. 5, the Laken Riley Act, on January 20, 2025 (Senate roll call vote 7). Excerpt: "On Passage of the Bill (S. 5, As Amended) … Merkley (D-OR), Nay" (U.S. Senate, https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote1191/vote_119_1_00007.htm)
[21] ENDORSEMENT (the endorser's opinion) by Oregon State Fire Fighters Council: Jeff Merkley's pamphlet statement lists Oregon State Fire Fighters Council as an endorser. Excerpt: "Endorsements: Oregon State Fire Fighters Council" (Oregon Voters' Pamphlet (Clackamas edition), p. 31, https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book14_web.pdf)
[22] ENDORSEMENT (the endorser's opinion) by OR Labor Federation, AFL-CIO: Jeff Merkley's pamphlet statement lists OR Labor Federation, AFL-CIO as an endorser. Excerpt: "OR Labor" (Oregon Voters' Pamphlet (Clackamas edition), p. 31, https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book14_web.pdf)
[23] ENDORSEMENT (the endorser's opinion) by Planned Parenthood Action Fund: Jeff Merkley's pamphlet statement lists Planned Parenthood Action Fund as an endorser. Excerpt: "Planned Parenthood Action Fund" (Oregon Voters' Pamphlet (Clackamas edition), p. 31, https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book14_web.pdf)
[24] ENDORSEMENT (the endorser's opinion) by Oregon League of Conservation Voters: Jeff Merkley's pamphlet statement lists Oregon League of Conservation Voters as an endorser. Excerpt: "League of Conservation Voters" (Oregon Voters' Pamphlet (Clackamas edition), p. 31, https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book14_web.pdf)
[25] ENDORSEMENT (the endorser's opinion) by Portland Mercury: Portland Mercury endorsed Jeff Merkley for US Senator. Excerpt: "US Senator: Jeff Merkley" (Portland Mercury, https://www.portlandmercury.com/election-2026/the-mercurys-2026-november-endorsement-cheat-sheet/)
[26] ENDORSEMENT (the endorser's opinion) by Willamette Week: Willamette Week endorsed Jeff Merkley for U.S. Senate. Excerpt: "Merkley has fought for this day during long, bleak months when it looked like Trump’s dark vision of blood-and-soil nationalism couldn’t be curtailed. He has earned a chance to hold Trump to account." (Willamette Week, https://www.wweek.com/news/2026/10/14/wws-fall-2026-endorsements-federal/)

[30] Henry's pamphlet statement calls for ending wars and cites the number of U.S. military bases abroad. Excerpt: "End Pointless Wars. [31] Henry proposes tripling the federal minimum wage of $7.25 an hour. Excerpt: "Triple the $7.25/hour minimum wage, same since 2009." ITEM: Governor (candidate race)

SIDE id="brett-smith" — Brett Smith, Pacific Green
[1] In his voters' pamphlet statement, Smith lists his occupation as inventor, small business owner, welder and fabricator. Excerpt: "Inventor, Small Business Owner, Welder, Fabricator" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[2] His pamphlet statement lists a welding apprenticeship and more than a decade of regulatory compliance work with the FDA and USPTO. Excerpt: "Toromont Energy Welding Apprenticeship, Over a decade of experience with regulatory compliance for the FDA and USPTO" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[3] His pamphlet statement lists no prior governmental experience. Excerpt: "None" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[4] Smith's pamphlet statement proposes a full audit of state systems and the tax code by independent contractors. Excerpt: "A full audit of our systems and tax code by independent contractors." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[5] Smith calls for healthcare for all and says the state has the money for it. Excerpt: "Healthcare for all. We have the money" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[6] Smith's statement opposes unconstitutional surveillance. Excerpt: "No unconstitutional surveillance" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[7] Smith proposes a permanent moratorium on data centers. Excerpt: "A permanent moratorium on data centers" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[8] Smith proposes a constitutional amendment stating no Oregonian will be drafted into a war not sanctioned by Congress. Excerpt: "A constitutional amendment to state no Oregonian will be drafted into a war not sanctioned by Congress" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[9] Smith supports subsidies for local businesses and ranchers rather than corporations. Excerpt: "Subsidies for local businesses and ranchers. Not corporations" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)

SIDE id="tina-kotek" — Tina Kotek, Democrat, incumbent
[10] The Oregon Blue Book says Kotek was elected governor on November 8, 2022, and sworn in as Oregon's 39th governor on January 9, 2023. Excerpt: "She was elected governor on November 8, 2022, and sworn in as Oregon's 39th governor on January 9, 2023." (Oregon Secretary of State, Oregon Blue Book, https://sos.oregon.gov/blue-book/Pages/state/executive/governor-bio.aspx)
[11] The Blue Book says she was first elected to represent North Portland in 2006. Excerpt: "She was first elected to represent North Portland in 2006." (Oregon Secretary of State, Oregon Blue Book, https://sos.oregon.gov/blue-book/Pages/state/executive/governor-bio.aspx)
[12] The Blue Book says she became the first openly lesbian speaker of any state house in the nation in 2013. Excerpt: "In 2013, she became the first openly lesbian speaker of any state house in the nation." (Oregon Secretary of State, Oregon Blue Book, https://sos.oregon.gov/blue-book/Pages/state/executive/governor-bio.aspx)
[13] Her voters' pamphlet statement lists past work at the Oregon Food Bank and Children First. Excerpt: "Oregon Food Bank, Children First" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[14] Kotek's pamphlet statement says she has raised the minimum wage, passed paid family leave and expanded health insurance coverage. Excerpt: "Tina has raised the minimum wage, passed paid family leave, and expanded health insurance coverage." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[15] Kotek's statement says she supports moratoriums on new data centers. Excerpt: "Tina supports moratoriums on new data centers" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[16] Kotek's statement says she is cutting red tape to build more affordable homes. Excerpt: "cutting red tape to build more affordable homes" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[17] Kotek's statement says she supports more learning time rather than shorter school years. Excerpt: "Tina is fighting for more learning time - not shorter school years." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[18] Kotek's statement says she declared a housing emergency and increased shelter and treatment beds. Excerpt: "Tina declared a housing emergency, increased shelter and treatment beds" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[19] Kotek's statement says she is focused on protecting basic rights. Excerpt: "Tina’s focused on protecting our basic rights." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[20] ENDORSEMENT (the endorser's opinion) by Planned Parenthood Action Oregon: Tina Kotek's pamphlet statement lists Planned Parenthood Action Oregon as an endorser. ITEM: US Representative, 3 (candidate race)

SIDE id="maxine-dexter" — Maxine E Dexter, Democrat, incumbent
[1] In her voters' pamphlet statement, Dexter lists her occupation as U.S. Representative. Excerpt: "U.S. Representative" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[2] Her pamphlet statement lists past work as a pulmonary and critical care physician and as a grocery worker. Excerpt: "Pulmonary/Critical Care Physician, Grocery Worker" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[3] Her pamphlet statement lists a B.A. and M.D. from the University of Washington. Excerpt: "University of Washington, B.A., M.D." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[4] Her official House biography says she was elected to the U.S. House in 2024. Excerpt: "In 2024, Dexter was honored to be elected to the U.S. House of Representatives." (Office of U.S. Rep. Maxine Dexter, https://dexter.house.gov/about)
[5] Her official biography says she practiced for over 15 years as a lung and critical care physician at Kaiser Permanente. Excerpt: "She practiced for over 15 years as a lung and critical care physician at Kaiser Permanente" (Office of U.S. Rep. Maxine Dexter, https://dexter.house.gov/about)
[6] Dexter's pamphlet statement calls healthcare a human right and supports high-quality, accessible and affordable care for all. Excerpt: "Healthcare is a human right: High quality, accessible and affordable care for all." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[7] Dexter's pamphlet statement lists good schools, living wages, union jobs, affordable housing and childcare among things she will continue fighting for. Excerpt: "Good schools, living wages, union jobs, affordable housing and childcare." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[8] Dexter's statement calls for no more wars, restoring humanitarian aid, expanding legal immigration and protecting clean air and water. Excerpt: "No more wars. Restore humanitarian aid. Expand legal immigration. Protect clean air and water." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[9] Dexter says she would protect voting rights, end corruption and get dark money out of politics. Excerpt: "Protect voting rights. End corruption. Defend our communities from authoritarianism. Get dark money out of politics." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[10] Dexter supports investing in clean, affordable, renewable energy. Excerpt: "Invest in clean, affordable, renewable energy." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)
[11] Dexter voted No on the House motion to concur in the Senate amendment to H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, on July 3, 2025 (Roll Call 190, 218-214). Excerpt: "QUESTION: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendment … BILL TITLE: One Big Beautiful Bill Act … ---- NOES 214 --- … Dexter" (Office of the Clerk, U.S. House of Representatives, https://clerk.house.gov/evs/2025/roll190)
[12] Dexter voted Nay on House passage of S. 5, the Laken Riley Act, on January 22, 2025 (Roll Call 23, 263-156). Excerpt: "Roll Call 23, Bill Number: S. 5, 119th Congress, 1st Session … On Passage … Laken Riley Act … Dexter Nay" (Office of the Clerk, U.S. House of Representatives, https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/2025023)

ITEM: County Commissioner Chair (candidate race)

SIDE id="shannon-singleton" — Shannon Singleton
[1] Singleton currently serves as Multnomah County's District 2 Commissioner. Excerpt: "District 2 Commissioner" (Multnomah County, https://multco.us/board)
[2] In her voters' pamphlet statement, Singleton lists her occupational background as housing policy director, executive director of JOIN, and social worker. Excerpt: "Housing Policy Director, Executive Director, JOIN, Social Worker" (Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print), https://multco.us/file/_large_print_multnomah_county_voters'_pamphlet_-_november_2026_general_election/download)
[3] Singleton's pamphlet statement lists bachelor's and master's degrees in social work. Excerpt: "BA, MA, Social Work" (Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print), https://multco.us/file/_large_print_multnomah_county_voters'_pamphlet_-_november_2026_general_election/download)
[4] Singleton's pamphlet statement lists prior service on A Home for Everyone Coordinating Board, the Portland Housing Advisory Commission and the Metro Housing Bond Oversight Committee. Excerpt: "A Home for Everyone Coordinating Board, Portland Housing Advisory Commission, Metro Housing Bond Oversight Committee" (Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print), https://multco.us/file/_large_print_multnomah_county_voters'_pamphlet_-_november_2026_general_election/download)
[5] Her county profile says Singleton served as housing policy advisor to Governor Kate Brown starting in 2019. Excerpt: "In 2019 Shannon joined Governor Kate Brown's administration as her housing policy advisor." (Multnomah County, https://multco.us/profile/shannon-singleton)
[6] In her voters' pamphlet statement, Singleton says her approach will find lasting solutions to the homelessness crisis, lower costs and support families. Excerpt: "That's how we find real, lasting solutions to our homelessness crisis, lower costs, and support families." (Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print), https://multco.us/file/_large_print_multnomah_county_voters'_pamphlet_-_november_2026_general_election/download)

[10] Singleton's campaign site says she wants to make Multnomah County a good place to own and run a business. Excerpt: "make Multnomah County a great place to own and run a business." (Friends of Shannon Singleton, https://www.shannonsingleton.org)

ITEM: County Auditor (candidate race)

SIDE id="nicole-pexton" — Nicole Pexton
[1] Pexton's candidate filing lists her current job as chief audit executive at the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission since 2022. Excerpt: "Chief Audit Executive, Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission (2022 to present)" (Multnomah County Elections (candidate filing), https://multco.us/file/nicole_pexton_candidate_filing/download)
[2] Pexton's filing lists prior auditing roles as senior auditor at Metro and performance auditor at the Secretary of State. Excerpt: "Other government auditing experience: Senior Auditor, Metro (2019-2022); Performance Auditor, Secretary of State (2012-2014)." (Multnomah County Elections (candidate filing), https://multco.us/file/nicole_pexton_candidate_filing/download)
[3] Pexton's voters' pamphlet statement lists a master's in public policy from American University, a B.A. from Whitman College, and internal auditor certifications. Excerpt: "American University, M.P.P; Whitman College, B.A.; Certified Internal Auditor, Certification in Risk Management Assurance" (Multnomah County Elections (JCVP-01 voters' pamphlet statement), https://multco.us/file/multco_auditor_nicole_pexton/download)
[4] Pexton's pamphlet statement lists chairing the Multnomah County Library Bond Oversight Committee and the Department of Early Learning and Care Audit Committee. Excerpt: "Chair, Multnomah County Library Bond Oversight Committee; Chair, Department of Early Learning and Care Audit Committee;" (Multnomah County Elections (JCVP-01 voters' pamphlet statement), https://multco.us/file/multco_auditor_nicole_pexton/download)
[5] In her voters' pamphlet statement, Pexton says she will push for more transparent and accountable county governance. Excerpt: "As County Auditor, I will fight for more transparent and accountable governance." (Multnomah County Elections (JCVP-01 voters' pamphlet statement), https://multco.us/file/multco_auditor_nicole_pexton/download)
[6] Pexton's pamphlet statement says she will shorten the audit process so audits can improve as many services as possible. Excerpt: "I will shorten the audit process so our audits can improve as many services as possible." (Multnomah County Elections (JCVP-01 voters' pamphlet statement), https://multco.us/file/multco_auditor_nicole_pexton/download)
[7] Pexton's pamphlet statement says audit reports will be brief and target key risks with timely solutions. Excerpt: "Reports will be brief and target key risks with timely solutions." (Multnomah County Elections (JCVP-01 voters' pamphlet statement), https://multco.us/file/multco_auditor_nicole_pexton/download)
[8] Pexton's pamphlet statement says she will explore ways for auditors to give proactive support and advice to catch problems early. Excerpt: "I will explore ways for auditors to give proactive support and advice, so we can catch problems early." (Multnomah County Elections (JCVP-01 voters' pamphlet statement), https://multco.us/file/multco_auditor_nicole_pexton/download)
[9] Pexton's pamphlet statement says she wants residents to see results and know their tax dollars are well spent. Excerpt: "I want residents to see results; to know their tax dollars are well spent." ITEM: City Councilor, 3 (candidate race)

SIDE id="john-sweeney" — John Sweeney
[1] The Portland Mercury reports Sweeney is a retired Portland Parks & Recreation supervisor. Excerpt: "John Sweeney is a retired Portland Parks & Recreation supervisor." (Portland Mercury, https://www.portlandmercury.com/election-2026/meet-the-candidates-for-city-council-district-3/)
[2] The Portland Mercury reports Sweeney is a retired captain in the Oregon Army National Guard. Excerpt: "He’s also a retired captain in the Oregon Army National Guard." (Portland Mercury, https://www.portlandmercury.com/election-2026/meet-the-candidates-for-city-council-district-3/)
[3] OPB describes Sweeney as a mechanical designer who wants the city to deliver better on its taxes. Excerpt: "John Sweeney is a mechanical designer who wants the city to deliver better on its taxes" (OPB, https://www.opb.org/article/2026/10/07/what-to-know-about-portland-district-3-council-race/)
[4] In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Sweeney lists saving city services by lowering taxes in downtown Portland as a priority. Excerpt: "Saving city services by lowering taxes in downtown Portland." (Portland Tribune, https://portlandtribune.com/2026/10/13/meet-the-portland-city-council-district-3-candidates-their-priorities-experience-and-fun-facts/)

[172] Hallett's pamphlet statement lists prior service as deputy probate clerk at the Muscogee County Probate Court. Excerpt: "Deputy Probate Clerk, Muscogee County Probate Court" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_matthias_hallett/download)
[173] In his voters' pamphlet statement, Hallett says police should be present, visible and known in the neighborhoods they serve. Excerpt: "Police should be present, visible, and known in the neighborhoods they serve" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_matthias_hallett/download)
[174] Hallett's pamphlet statement says Portland cannot tax its way out of a shrinking base and must grow it back. Excerpt: "We cannot tax our way out of a shrinking base; we must grow it back." (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_matthias_hallett/download)
[175] Hallett's pamphlet statement says he will set strict permitting timelines with automatic escalation when projects stall. Excerpt: "I will set strict permitting timelines with automatic escalation when projects stall" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_matthias_hallett/download)
[176] Hallett's pamphlet statement calls for right-sizing the business tax structure to keep Portland competitive. Excerpt: "right-size the business tax structure to keep us competitive" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_matthias_hallett/download)
[177] Hallett's pamphlet statement calls for targeting manufacturing and traded-sector employers that bring outside dollars into the economy. Excerpt: "target manufacturing and traded-sector employers that bring outside dollars into our economy" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_matthias_hallett/download)
[178] In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Hallett says homelessness contracts should pay for outcomes such as people housed and staying housed. Excerpt: "Homelessness contracts should pay for outcomes: people housed and remaining housed, not just contacts made." (Portland Tribune, https://portlandtribune.com/2026/10/13/meet-the-portland-city-council-district-3-candidates-their-priorities-experience-and-fun-facts/)

SIDE id="kellie-torres" — Kellie Torres
[179] Torres's city candidate filing form lists her occupation as external affairs and partnerships manager at Portland Parks & Recreation. Excerpt: "External Affairs & Partnerships Manager, Portland Parks & Recreation" (City of Portland Auditor's Office, Elections, https://www.portland.gov/auditor/elections/documents/torres-kellie-2026-aud-120-form/download)
[180] Torres's filing form lists past work as chief of staff for Commissioner Dan Ryan. Excerpt: "Chief of Staff for Commissioner Dan Ryan, City of Portland" (City of Portland Auditor's Office, Elections, https://www.portland.gov/auditor/elections/documents/torres-kellie-2026-aud-120-form/download)
[181] OPB reports Torres has worked for the city on and off since 2005. Excerpt: "Torres has worked for the city on and off since 2005" (OPB, https://www.opb.org/article/2026/10/07/what-to-know-about-portland-district-3-council-race/)
[182] OPB reports Torres is focused on strengthening city parks and fully funding public safety programs. Excerpt: "She’s focused on strengthening city parks, fully funding public safety programs" (OPB, https://www.opb.org/article/2026/10/07/what-to-know-about-portland-district-3-council-race/)
[183] The Portland Mercury reports Torres is focused on small businesses, economic vitality and housing affordability. Excerpt: "She’s focused on small businesses, economic vitality, and housing affordability" (Portland Mercury, https://www.portlandmercury.com/election-2026/meet-the-candidates-for-city-council-district-3/)
[184] In a Portland Mercury candidate profile, Torres says Portland needs practical, progressive leaders who can move from conversation to action. Excerpt: "I’m running because Portland needs practical, progressive leaders who know how to move from conversation to action," (Portland Mercury, https://www.portlandmercury.com/election-2026/meet-the-candidates-for-city-council-district-3/)
[185] In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Torres says city government should set clear goals, measure results and be transparent about what works. Excerpt: "City government should set clear goals, measure results and be transparent about what is working and what isn’t." (Portland Tribune, https://portlandtribune.com/2026/10/13/meet-the-portland-city-council-district-3-candidates-their-priorities-experience-and-fun-facts/)
[186] ENDORSEMENT (the endorser's opinion) by Willamette Week: Willamette Week ranked Kellie Torres #3 for Portland City Council District 3. Excerpt: "We didn’t find her all that inspiring, nor were her policy ideas terribly original, but we think she’ll provide a common-sense vote to safeguard the city’s basic services from budget cuts as the city approaches another $100 million-plus deficit." (Willamette Week, https://www.wweek.com/news/2026/10/14/wws-fall-2026-endorsements-portland-city-council/)

SIDE id="kimberly-tucker" — Kimberly Tucker
[187] Tucker's city candidate filing form lists her occupation as board certified behavior analyst at Kadiant since 2026. Excerpt: "Board Certified Behavior Analyst, Kadiant, 2026-present" (City of Portland Auditor's Office, Elections, https://www.portland.gov/auditor/elections/documents/tucker-kimberly-aud-120/download)
[188] The Portland Mercury reports Tucker specializes in behavioral analysis and special education. Excerpt: "Kimberly Tucker specializes in behavioral analysis and special education." (Portland Mercury, https://www.portlandmercury.com/election-2026/meet-the-candidates-for-city-council-district-3/)
[189] The Portland Tribune reports Tucker withdrew her campaign due to personal circumstances. Excerpt: "Kimberly Tucker withdrew her campaign due to personal circumstances." (Portland Tribune, https://portlandtribune.com/2026/10/13/meet-the-portland-city-council-district-3-candidates-their-priorities-experience-and-fun-facts/)

SIDE id="cristal-otero" — Cristal Otero
[190] Otero's voters' pamphlet statement lists a background in homeless services and city and county government. Excerpt: "Homeless Services; City and County Government" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_cristal_otero/download)
[191] Otero's pamphlet statement lists an MSW from Portland State University, an MA from Pacific Northwest College of Art and a BA from The Evergreen State College. Excerpt: "MSW, Portland State University; MA, Pacific Northwest College of Art; BA, The Evergreen State College" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_cristal_otero/download)
[192] Otero's pamphlet statement lists service as a Mark O. Hatfield Fellow with the City of Fairview and as a senior program specialist in Multnomah County homeless services. Excerpt: "Mark O. Hatfield Fellow, City of Fairview; Program Specialist Senior, Homeless Services, Multnomah County" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_cristal_otero/download)
[193] The Portland Mercury reports Otero has eight years of direct-service experience with homeless residents. Excerpt: "Otero has eight years of experience working in direct service with homeless residents" (Portland Mercury, https://www.portlandmercury.com/election-2026/meet-the-candidates-for-city-council-district-3/)
[194] In her voters' pamphlet statement, Otero says she will judge major projects and borrowing by their monthly cost to Portlanders. Excerpt: "I will judge major projects and borrowing by what they cost Portlanders each month." (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_cristal_otero/download)
[195] Otero's pamphlet statement says Portland should set a goal to end homelessness for people with intellectual disabilities and brain injuries. Excerpt: "Portland should set a concrete goal: end homelessness for people with intellectual disabilities and brain injuries" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_cristal_otero/download)
[196] Otero's pamphlet statement proposes letting some publicly supported apartment buildings transition to resident ownership and management. Excerpt: "some publicly supported apartment buildings can transition to resident ownership and management" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_cristal_otero/download)
[197] Otero's pamphlet statement says she will back prevailing wages, apprenticeships and labor standards on public projects. Excerpt: "I will back prevailing wages, apprenticeships, safe working conditions, and labor standards on public projects." (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_cristal_otero/download)
[198] Otero's pamphlet statement says the Portland Clean Energy Fund should fund climate work, not budget gaps. Excerpt: "PCEF should fund climate work, not budget gaps." (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_cristal_otero/download)
[199] Otero's pamphlet statement says she will reduce seismic risk at the Critical Energy Infrastructure Hub. Excerpt: "I will reduce seismic risk at the Critical Energy Infrastructure Hub" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_cristal_otero/download)
[200] In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Otero says she wants to expand housing production while giving neighborhoods more say over its speed, style and density. Excerpt: "I want to expand housing production while giving neighborhoods more say over the speed, style and density of change;" (Portland Tribune, https://portlandtribune.com/2026/10/13/meet-the-portland-city-council-district-3-candidates-their-priorities-experience-and-fun-facts/)
[201] ENDORSEMENT (the endorser's opinion) by Sierra Club Oregon Chapter: Cristal Otero's pamphlet statement lists Sierra Club Oregon Chapter as an endorser. Excerpt: "ENDORSED BY: Sierra Club Oregon Chapter" (Multnomah County Voters' Pamphlet, p. 59, https://multco.us/file/multnomah_county_voters'_pamphlet_-_november_2026_general_election/download)
[202] ENDORSEMENT (the endorser's opinion) by Willamette Week: Willamette Week ranked Cristal Otero #4 for Portland City Council District 3. Excerpt: "She’s like a skilled plumber, but for homelessness spending. We would rank her fourth." (Willamette Week, https://www.wweek.com/news/2026/10/14/wws-fall-2026-endorsements-portland-city-council/)

SIDE id="guy-frankenstein" — Guy Frankenstein
[203] Frankenstein's city candidate filing form lists his current occupation as student. Excerpt: "Student" (City of Portland Auditor's Office, Elections, https://www.portland.gov/auditor/elections/documents/frankenstein-guy-aud-120-original/download)
[204] The Portland Mercury reports Frankenstein has a background in auto insurance and is currently in graduate school. Excerpt: "Frankenstein, 43, has a background in auto insurance, but is currently in grad school." (Portland Mercury, https://www.portlandmercury.com/election-2026/meet-the-candidates-for-city-council-district-3/)
[205] In a Portland Mercury candidate profile, Frankenstein says he has no previous political experience and no desire to work within politics. Excerpt: "I have no previous political experience and have absolutely no desire to work within politics" (Portland Mercury, https://www.portlandmercury.com/election-2026/meet-the-candidates-for-city-council-district-3/)
[206] In a Portland Mercury candidate profile, Frankenstein says he is not running to be an effective team player. Excerpt: "I’m not running for City Council to be an effective team player." (Portland Mercury, https://www.portlandmercury.com/election-2026/meet-the-candidates-for-city-council-district-3/)

SIDE id="keir-legree" — Keir Legree
[207] Legree's voters' pamphlet statement lists 30 years as general manager of Savoy Studios and founding PlanXT. Excerpt: "General Manager, Savoy Studios (30 years); Founder, PlanXT" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_keir-legree/download)
[208] Legree's pamphlet statement lists a high school diploma from Rex Putnam High School. Excerpt: "Rex Putnam High School, High School Diploma" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_keir-legree/download)
[209] The Portland Mercury describes Savoy Studios, which Legree manages, as a lighting and art glass studio. Excerpt: "Legree, 54, is the general manager of Savoy Studios, a lighting and art glass studio." (Portland Mercury, https://www.portlandmercury.com/election-2026/meet-the-candidates-for-city-council-district-3/)
[210] In his voters' pamphlet statement, Legree says he has a plan and the city needs to work on ending street homelessness. Excerpt: "I have a plan, we need to work on ending street homelessness." (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_keir-legree/download)
[211] Legree's pamphlet statement calls for hiring more police officers and 911 dispatchers to improve response times. Excerpt: "hiring more police officers and 911 dispatchers to improve response times" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_keir-legree/download)
[212] Legree's pamphlet statement says he will work to reduce infrastructure project costs and lower utility bills. Excerpt: "I will work to reduce ongoing infrastructure project costs and lower our bills" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_keir-legree/download)
[213] In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Legree calls street homelessness Portland's most urgent problem. Excerpt: "Street homelessness is Portland’s most urgent problem, affecting just about every other issue we face." (Portland Tribune, https://portlandtribune.com/2026/10/13/meet-the-portland-city-council-district-3-candidates-their-priorities-experience-and-fun-facts/)
[214] In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Legree calls for a compassionate approach that expects progress in exchange for services and treatment. Excerpt: "We need a new approach that is compassionate but also expects progress in exchange for services and treatment." (Portland Tribune, https://portlandtribune.com/2026/10/13/meet-the-portland-city-council-district-3-candidates-their-priorities-experience-and-fun-facts/)

SIDE id="esther-leon" — Esther Leon
[215] León's voters' pamphlet statement lists her occupation as physical therapist and community college professor. Excerpt: "Physical Therapist; Community College Professor" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_esther_leon/download)
[216] León's pamphlet statement lists a BA in kinesiology and nutrition from Whittier College and a doctorate in physical therapy from the University of Southern California. Excerpt: "Whittier College, BA in Kinesiology & Nutrition; University of Southern California, Doctorate in Physical Therapy" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_esther_leon/download)
[217] OPB reports León is a physical therapist who works in Oregon prisons and qualifies for the city's donation-matching program. Excerpt: "Esther León is a physical therapist who works in Oregon prisons and is also qualified for the donation-matching program." (OPB, https://www.opb.org/article/2026/10/07/what-to-know-about-portland-district-3-council-race/)
[218] León's voters' pamphlet statement calls for a vacancy tax on corporate landlords to fund affordable housing. Excerpt: "Implement a vacancy tax on corporate landlords that funnels into affordable housing" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_esther_leon/download)
[219] León's pamphlet statement calls for fully funding Portland Street Response for 24/7 citywide dispatch. Excerpt: "Full funding of Portland Street Response for 24/7, city-wide dispatch" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_esther_leon/download)
[220] León's pamphlet statement calls for a moratorium on AI data centers. Excerpt: "Moratorium on AI Data Centers" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_esther_leon/download)
[221] León's pamphlet statement proposes exploring universal basic income for artists. Excerpt: "Invest in the Arts: explore universal basic income for artists" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_esther_leon/download)
[222] León's pamphlet statement calls for fully auditing use of public dollars and holding mishandlers accountable. Excerpt: "Fully audit use of public dollars; hold mishandlers accountable" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_esther_leon/download)
[223] León's pamphlet statement calls for revoking the ICE facility permit, framing it as standing up to fascism. Excerpt: "Stand up to fascism: revoke the ICE facility permit" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_esther_leon/download)
[224] In a Portland Tribune Q&A, León says the city should look at raising the Portland Clean Energy Fund surcharge by another 1%. Excerpt: "We should look at raising the PCEF surcharge by another 1%" (Portland Tribune, https://portlandtribune.com/2026/10/13/meet-the-portland-city-council-district-3-candidates-their-priorities-experience-and-fun-facts/)

SIDE id="kenneth-landgraver-iii" — Kenneth (Kent) R Landgraver III
[225] Landgraver's voters' pamphlet statement lists his occupation as scientific instrument technician for the State of Oregon. Excerpt: "Scientific Instrument Technician; State of Oregon" (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_kenneth_kent_r_landgraver_iii/download)
[226] Landgraver's pamphlet statement lists work as a civilian electronics mechanic for the Oregon Army National Guard and as an electronics operations manager. Excerpt: "Electronics Mechanic (civilian), Oregon Army National Guard; Operations Manager, Electronics manufacturer & service." (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_kenneth_kent_r_landgraver_iii/download)
[227] Landgraver's city filing form lists 31 years in the Oregon Army National Guard, now retired. Excerpt: "Oregon Army National Guard - 31 years - Retired" (City of Portland Auditor's Office, Elections, https://www.portland.gov/auditor/elections/documents/landgraver-kenenth-2026-aud-120-form-original/download)
[228] In his voters' pamphlet statement, Landgraver says council votes affecting the city should be unanimous. Excerpt: "Council votes affecting the city should be unanimous." (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_kenneth_kent_r_landgraver_iii/download)
[229] Landgraver's pamphlet statement says he wants to stop what he calls the rebranding of the old commission system. Excerpt: "I want to stop the rebranding of the old commission system." (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_kenneth_kent_r_landgraver_iii/download)
[230] Landgraver's pamphlet statement says his goal is to ensure every tax dollar goes to doing the people's work. Excerpt: "My goal is to ensure every tax dollar goes to doing the people’s work." (Multnomah County Elections Division, https://multco.us/file/portland_dist_3_kenneth_kent_r_landgraver_iii/download)
[231] In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Landgraver says he wants to right-size sworn officers and integrate supportive services with mental health and street medicine. Excerpt: "I want to right-size sworn officers and integrate supportive services with mental health and street medicine." (Portland Tribune, https://portlandtribune.com/2026/10/13/meet-the-portland-city-council-district-3-candidates-their-priorities-experience-and-fun-facts/)

SIDE id="diane-sykes" — Diane S Sykes

Excerpt: "Northwest Oregon Labor Council" (Oregon Voters' Pamphlet, Multnomah edition, p. 59, https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book13_web.pdf)

pack.title: Measure 26-267: Amends Charter: Portland residents decide 2% of city's annual discretionary budget. (City of Portland)

background.statement: Summary: A citizen-initiated Portland charter amendment requiring the City Council to allocate an amount equal to at least 2% of the city's adopted General Fund discretionary ongoing expenses to a participatory budgeting program. Residents could propose citywide or district projects; city staff and budget delegates would refine proposals, and residents would make binding selections. An oversight committee of residents would help develop the program, which would start July 2027.

A YES vote: A yes vote amends the Portland City Charter to create a participatory budgeting program in which residents make binding decisions on spending an amount equal to at least 2% of the city's discretionary budget.
A NO vote: A no vote leaves the current budget process unchanged, in which the Mayor proposes and the Council amends and adopts the budget.

Fiscal impact: Under a recent forecast, the ballot summary gives a preliminary estimate of $16.4 million in FY 2027-28 and $17.0 million in FY 2028-29 to be allocated to the program; Council may identify funding from the entire city budget to meet the obligation.

ITEM: US Representative, 6 (candidate race)

SIDE id="andrea-salinas" — Andrea Salinas, Democrat, incumbent
[1] In her voters' pamphlet statement, Salinas lists her occupation as U.S. congresswoman. Excerpt: "U.S. Congresswoman" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Marion County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book8_web.pdf)
[2] Her pamphlet statement lists prior service as an Oregon state representative and on the Oregon Complete Count Committee, PEBB and the Oregon Commission on Hispanic Affairs. Excerpt: "Oregon State Representative, Oregon Complete Count Committee, PEBB Member, Oregon Commission on Hispanic Affairs" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Marion County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book8_web.pdf)
[3] Her pamphlet statement lists a BA from the University of California, Berkeley. Excerpt: "University of California, Berkeley, BA" (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Marion County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book8_web.pdf)
[4] Her official House page says she serves on the House Agriculture and Science, Space, and Technology committees. Excerpt: "Andrea is proud to serve on the House Agriculture and House Science, Space, and Technology Committees" (Office of U.S. Rep. Andrea Salinas, https://salinas.house.gov/about)
[5] Her official page says she previously worked as a congressional aide and policy advisor to Senator Harry Reid and Congressman Pete Stark. Excerpt: "as a US congressional aide and policy advisor to Senator Harry Reid and Congressman Pete Stark" (Office of U.S. Rep. Andrea Salinas, https://salinas.house.gov/about)
[6] Salinas's pamphlet statement says many Oregonians are struggling with expenses. Excerpt: "Andrea knows too many Oregonians are struggling with expenses." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Marion County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book8_web.pdf)
[7] Salinas says she is working to cap prescription drug costs and strengthen hospital price transparency. Excerpt: "Andrea is fighting to cap the cost of prescription drugs, strengthen price transparency at hospitals," (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Marion County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book8_web.pdf)
[8] Salinas's statement says she worked to secure federal funding for housing projects. Excerpt: "she fought to secure federal funding for housing projects," (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Marion County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book8_web.pdf)
[9] Salinas says she will protect abortion access and LGBTQ+ rights. Excerpt: "Andrea will always fight to protect abortion access and LGBTQ+ rights." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Marion County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book8_web.pdf)
[10] Salinas's statement says the main responsibility of members of Congress is to defend Americans' rights and freedoms. Excerpt: "The paramount responsibility of members of Congress is to defend American rights and freedoms." (Oregon Secretary of State, Nov 3 2026 Voters' Pamphlet (Marion County edition), https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book8_web.pdf)
[11] Salinas voted No on the House motion to concur in the Senate amendment to H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, on July 3, 2025 (Roll Call 190, 218-214). Excerpt: "QUESTION: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendment … BILL TITLE: One Big Beautiful Bill Act … ---- NOES 214 --- … Salinas" (Office of the Clerk, U.S. House of Representatives, https://clerk.house.gov/evs/2025/roll190)
[12] Salinas voted Nay on House passage of S. 5, the Laken Riley Act, on January 22, 2025 (Roll Call 23, 263-156). Excerpt: "Roll Call 23, Bill Number: S. 5, 119th Congress, 1st Session … On Passage … Laken Riley Act … Salinas Nay" (Office of the Clerk, U.S. House of Representatives, https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/2025023)
[13] ENDORSEMENT (the endorser's opinion) by Planned Parenthood Action Fund: Andrea Salinas's pamphlet statement lists Planned Parenthood Action Fund as an endorser. Excerpt: "Planned Parenthood Action Fund" (Oregon Voters' Pamphlet (Clackamas edition), p. 36, https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book14_web.pdf)
[14] ENDORSEMENT (the endorser's opinion) by Oregon League of Conservation Voters: Andrea Salinas's pamphlet statement lists Oregon League of Conservation Voters as an endorser. Excerpt: "Oregon League of Conservation Voters" (Oregon Voters' Pamphlet (Clackamas edition), p. 36, https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book14_web.pdf)
[15] ENDORSEMENT (the endorser's opinion) by Oregon Nurses Association: Andrea Salinas's pamphlet statement lists Oregon Nurses Association as an endorser. Excerpt: "Oregon Nurses Association" (Oregon Voters' Pamphlet (Clackamas edition), p. 36, https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Voters-Pamphlet/Documents/VP_G26-Book14_web.pdf)
[16] ENDORSEMENT (the endorser's opinion) by OR Labor Federation AFL-CIO: Andrea Salinas's pamphlet statement lists OR Labor Federation AFL-CIO as an endorser. pack.title: Measure 34-354: City of King City Charter Modernization Amendment (City of King City)

background.statement: Summary: King City asks voters to amend and restate its 2006 city charter. The measure adds definitions, mirrors the League of Oregon Cities model charter, clarifies vacancies and councilor duties and prohibitions, removes the prohibition on councilor compensation, adds a charter review section, and moves duties of the City Manager, Judge and City Attorney to ordinance or resolution. It keeps the council-manager form and the current way of selecting the mayor.
A YES vote: A yes vote amends and restates the King City charter as described in the ballot title.
A NO vote: A no vote leaves the current King City charter in effect.
Fiscal impact: The ballot title and explanatory statement give no cost or revenue estimate. The measure would remove the charter's prohibition on compensation for councilors.

facts.statement: Vincent Arditi argues the amendment does not change the present system in which the city council chooses the mayor, and urges a no vote so residents can vote for their mayor.

measure:king-city-34-354.sourcesText:
ITEM: Measure 34-354: City of King City Charter Modernization Amendment (City of King City) (ballot measure)

OFFICIAL BACKGROUND (neutral; any side may cite):
[1] Summary: King City asks voters to amend and restate its 2006 city charter. The measure adds definitions, mirrors the League of Oregon Cities model charter, clarifies vacancies and councilor duties and prohibitions, removes the prohibition on councilor compensation, adds a charter review section, and moves duties of the City Manager, Judge and City Attorney to ordinance or resolution. It keeps the council-manager form and the current way of selecting the mayor. (Official measure record, https://www.washingtoncountyor.gov/elections/documents/34-354-city-king-city-charter-modernization-amendment/download?inline)
[2] A YES vote: A yes vote amends and restates the King City charter as described in the ballot title. (Official measure record, https://www.washingtoncountyor.gov/elections/documents/34-354-city-king-city-charter-modernization-amendment/download?inline)
[3] A NO vote: A no vote leaves the current King City charter in effect. (Official measure record, https://www.washingtoncountyor.gov/elections/documents/34-354-city-king-city-charter-modernization-amendment/download?inline)
[4] Fiscal impact: The ballot title and explanatory statement give no cost or revenue estimate. The measure would remove the charter's prohibition on compensation for councilors. (Official measure record, https://www.washingtoncountyor.gov/elections/documents/34-354-city-king-city-charter-modernization-amendment/download?inline)

SIDE id="yes" — The case for YES
(no sourced statements on record)

SIDE id="no" — The case for NO
[5] Vincent Arditi argues the amendment does not change the present system in which the city council chooses the mayor, and urges a no vote so residents can vote for their mayor. Excerpt: "4 out of 7 council members still control their choice for your mayor as selected by city council." (Washington County Elections (Nov 3, 2026 Voters' Pamphlet, p. WC-58), https://www.washingtoncountyor.gov/elections/documents/november-3-2026-voters-pamphlet/download?inline)
[6] ENDORSEMENT (the endorser's opinion) by Vincent Arditi: Vincent Arditi furnished the only argument in opposition printed in the county voters' pamphlet. Excerpt: "This Information Furnished By: Vincent Arditi" (Washington County Elections (Nov 3, 2026 Voters' Pamphlet, p. WC-58), https://www.washingtoncountyor.gov/elections/documents/november-3-2026-voters-pamphlet/download?inline)
